Alternatively, consider binary. Define T_m (m butterflies) as the algorithm for size 2^m. T_1 = [1 1; 1 -1]. T_{m+1} is constructed as: first apply T_m in each half of the block (h=1,2,...,2^{m-1} butterflies act within each half-block of size 2^m), then do the h=2^m butterfly combining halves: for j in first half: (x[j], x[j+2^m]) = (x[j] + x[j+2^m], x[j] - x[j+2^m]).

By the induction hypothesis, after the first phase, x[j] = sum_{k < 2^m} (-1)^{popcount(j&k)} a[k] (within the upper half, k is from 0 to 2^m-1), and x[j + 2^m] = sum_{k<2^m} (-1)^{popcount(j&k)} a[k + 2^m].

So x_new[j'] = sum_{k0} (-1)^{popcount(j'&k0)} a[k0] + sum_{k0} (-1)^{popcount(j'&k0)} a[k0+2^m] = sum_k (-1)^{popcount(j' & k)} a[k]. ✓
